title: Five funds, four opened
subtitle: What one family owns, counted twice
note: The family is Antevo’s example household, with three made-up banks. Funds and companies are described, not named. Every figure is the Antevo Wealth tool’s answer on the date shown.

tries.label: Before and after the funds are opened
tries.source: Antevo Wealth, 25 Nov 2026. Shares of everything the family has recorded: CHF 35.5m.

items.name: Technology
evidence: As the statements show it: 39.6% of everything
With the funds opened: 46.1%
CHF 14.1m held directly, CHF 2.3m inside funds

items.name: America
evidence: As the statements show it: 88.1%, because four of the funds are American funds
With the funds opened: 81.4%
The funds hold companies in more than sixty countries

items.name: Switzerland
evidence: As the statements show it: 11.9%
With the funds opened: 15.4%
One American fund holds only Swiss companies

items.name: Funds opened
evidence: A world fund, a Nasdaq fund, a US bank fund and a Swiss fund: CHF 7.2m, 20.4% of everything
The US bank fund sits in two portfolios and is counted once

items.name: Not opened
evidence: A bond fund has no industry: it is counted as one holding
It is 12.8% of everything, and is left out of the industry shares

items.do: Read both counts side by side
items.why: The gap between them is what sits inside your funds.

items.do: Look for the same kind of company held twice
items.why: A world fund and a Nasdaq fund both hold large American technology companies, which the family also owns directly.

items.do: Check where a fund is from against what it holds
items.why: A fund listed in one country can hold companies from another. The factsheet lists its largest holdings by name.

items.do: Write down the share you are at ease with in one industry and one country
items.why: The page shows where things stand; the line is yours and your adviser’s to draw.

items.do: Ask what it would cost in a bad year
items.why: The same holdings, set against today’s risks.

sections.title: Banks and health care
sections.so_what: Broad funds add a little of everything, and most of all to what was already large.
evidence: Financial companies: 10.5% as the statements show it, 12.3% with the funds opened
Health care: 8.4%, then 10.6%

sections.title: Held directly and inside funds
sections.so_what: You can see how much of a share comes from your own choices and how much arrived inside a fund.
evidence: Technology: CHF 14.1m held directly, CHF 2.3m inside funds
Switzerland: CHF 4.2m held directly, CHF 1.3m inside funds

sections.title: What the count covers
sections.verdict: 87% of the money has an industry
sections.so_what: What is not classified is left out of the shares, not counted as zero.
evidence: With the funds opened: the industry is known for 87.2% of the money
As the statements show it: 70.3%
By country: all of it

sections.title: The limit
sections.verdict: By industry and country, not by company
sections.so_what: For the names inside a fund, read its factsheet. This page shows the shape, not the list.
evidence: Funds are opened by industry and by country, not company by company. A fund with no published breakdown stays closed and is counted as one holding; the answer names the funds it opened.

links.text: Two funds at two banks hold large American technology companies; the family holds the same kind directly at a third. Technology is larger than any one statement shows.
A fund counts as American on a statement because it is listed there. Opened, one of them is entirely Swiss.

watch: The share of technology with the funds opened, at each review
Any new fund: was it opened, or did it stay closed?
The gap between the two counts: it grows when funds and single shares overlap
disclaimer: From the Antevo Wealth tool’s answers on the date shown. Funds are opened by industry and by country, not company by company. A fund with no published breakdown stays closed and is counted as one holding; the answer names the funds it opened. The page describes where the money sits; it is not investment advice and says nothing about what to buy or sell.
